value.rationale: Frozen measurement directions create a natural restricted stochastic-design problem not answered by unconstrained equal-angle optimality. The theorem identifies a structural threshold: one added direction admits a single optimum valid for every risk threshold, whereas two directions can force incompatibility between low-order dispersion and rare-event tails. The competing designs remain separated on an open interval of original angles, not just one numerical accident. It supplies an actionable boundary on the utility of stochastic dominance in planar Gaussian sensor augmentation.
